prompts_findings.prompt_lead: Download the AE101 content tarball to `~/Downloads/ae101-content.tar.gz` using c

risks_fired.evidence: Single primary curl action plus a conditional 401-retry branch; a brief 'I'll download that now' opener is possible in a minority of runs but non-disruptive on a housekeeping step.
risks_fired.fix_hint: No edit needed — preamble on a setup-only prompt doesn't cost learning; manual-download fallback already covers curl failure.

prompts_findings.prompt_lead: I'm starting a six-module training called Agentic Engineering 101. Walk these in

risks_fired.evidence: In-fence 'no preamble' is present, but the prompt opens with a scene-setting sentence ('I'm starting a six-module training called Agentic Engineering 101') before the 3 numbered steps — that framing reliably invites a confirmatory opener despite the suppressor.
risks_fired.fix_hint: Optional body primer above the prompt: 'Claude may open with a short summary line before Step 1 — that's fine, watch the per-step output.' Non-blocking.

risks_fired.evidence: CARVE-OUT APPLIED (fresh-install-context, memory/compounded/2026-05-24-prompts-overwrite-anxiety-fresh-install-carveout.md). Step 3 installs three skills to ~/.claude/skills/ and Step 1 creates ~/Documents/ae101-content with no explicit overwrite directive, but this is curriculum-delivered prework onboarding: body says 'The curated security skills install in Step 4,' install target is ~/.claude/skills/, and this is the student's first encounter with the bundle. The collision-pause path is not the modal case.
risks_fired.fix_hint: Carve-out satisfied — no edit required; adding an overwrite directive would imply a collision norm that doesn't exist on a fresh-install path.

risks_fired.evidence: 'Report success on each step and tell me what you did' invites self-summary, but each step already carries a concrete, falsifiable check baked into the fence (named subfolders present, absolute skill paths named) rather than a qualitative self-grade.
risks_fired.fix_hint: Defer; tighten 'tell me what you did' to 'tell me what you wrote' (the confirmed paths) per check_prompts §21 only if cohort feedback shows install confusion.

risks_fired.evidence: 'Use ~/Documents/ae101-content unless there is a good reason not to' offers a default the student isn't prompted to scrutinize — low stakes (a directory-naming convention, not a pedagogical choice) and the path is the one later modules' artefact contracts assume.
risks_fired.fix_hint: No edit needed; the offered default is intentional and matches the artefact-contract table other modules read from.

prompts_findings.prompt_lead: Walk these in order, ask one question at a time if you need to, no preamble.

risks_fired.evidence: CARVE-OUT APPLIED (memory/compounded/2026-04-27-prompts-question-dump.md). In-fence 'ask one question at a time if you need to' plus TWO body callouts satisfy the carve-out shape verbatim: pre-prompt names failure mode + recovery ('push back if it dumps all four criteria at once. One bug at a time, then the next.'); post-prompt names the AskUserQuestion tool + one-at-a-time alternative + student agency ('ask Claude to use the AskUserQuestion tool, or to give you the candidate-bug screen one bug at a time. Whichever reads better.').
risks_fired.fix_hint: Carve-out satisfied — no edit required; body callouts already name the failure mode, the recovery, and give the student agency.

risks_fired.evidence: 'no preamble' explicit; Step 1 itself opens by asking the student a question, which naturally suppresses plan-talk. Residual courtesy-bridge risk in a minority of runs.

'Help me pick the most trivial-and-visible one' risks rubber-stamping the student's first instinct; partially offset by the adjacent body callout reinforcing the size bar ('Trivial means a few lines here and there, not a multi-file refactor').
risks_fired.fix_hint: Optional: add 'if the bug looks bigger than 50 lines once you look at it, say so and ask for another candidate' to Step 1 to close the rubber-stamp path fully.

risks_fired.evidence: Step 2's readiness read (tests run, git status, PR-ready) is self-reported, but the fence's closing clause ('Flag anything that would get in my way') actively invites a problem-list rather than a clean bill of health, which counters charity.
risks_fired.fix_hint: Optional: add 'confirm I can push a branch and open a PR on this remote, not just that git is clean locally' to Step 2 to catch remote-side blockers the local git-status check misses.

prompts_findings.prompt_lead: Use the AskUserQuestion tool for speeding up screening and making suggestions. O

risks_fired.evidence: One-liner tool-switch command; a brief 'Sure, switching to AskUserQuestion' opener is possible but compliance with the actual instruction is near-certain and any narration is minimal.
risks_fired.fix_hint: No edit needed — this prompt is itself a question-dump mitigation, not a risk vector worth hardening further.
